methodology.aggregation: median of per-block aggregate throughput, with min and max across the same blocks
methodology.cross_thread_backpressure: bounded per-worker mailbox; a producer facing a full mailbox frees the block itself rather than blocking, and the fallback count is published
methodology.operation_stream: seeded random operation stream; each operation, size, and slot is drawn from a splitmix64 stream that never observes allocator behavior
methodology.oversubscription: thread points are literal worker counts 1/4/16; points above the allowed logical CPU count are labeled oversubscribed and describe contention, not core scaling
methodology.pairing: all four allocators run the same frozen per-worker operation count and the same stream inside one block, in a rotated near-balanced order
methodology.rigor: coverage mode - reduced statistical rigor (3 blocks)
methodology.seed_chain: splitmix64 chain over (run seed, pattern tag, thread count, block, worker); the allocator is deliberately absent so all four allocators replay one stream
methodology.statistics_omitted: no bootstrap confidence intervals and no noise gating; three blocks cannot support them and the panel says so
methodology.work_normalization: operations per worker are calibrated once per (pattern, thread point) against upstream-mimalloc and frozen across allocators; total work scales with worker count

sampling.method: polled while the measured block runs; the peak over the block is retained
sampling.source: external /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup Rss, parsed as integer kB * 1024

methodology.baseline_definition: external RSS/HWM after child warmup and baseline-ready, before begin
methodology.fragmentation_formula: (sampled_peak_rss_bytes - baseline_rss_bytes) / peak_live_requested_bytes; both operands must be positive
methodology.hwm_discrepancy_tolerance: flag when abs(sampled RSS delta - VmHWM delta) > max(8 MiB, 20% of the larger positive delta)
methodology.hwm_source: /proc/<pid>/status VmHWM, parsed as integer kB * 1024; cross-check only
methodology.page_touch_contract: every allocation touches deterministic boundary bytes and at least one byte per OS page
methodology.post_drain_definition: external smaps_rollup RSS at >=100ms, >=1s, and >=5s after workload-drained
methodology.purge_policy: natural allocator behavior only; no allocator-specific purge call
methodology.sampled_peak_definition: maximum external smaps_rollup RSS timestamped inside workload-active..workload-drained
